Docs/Parallel environments

Parallel environments

Scale the native-scene matrix through independent processes while retaining the registered evaluation contract.

One native-scene environment per process

make_scene_eval_env enforces num_envs=1 and sim_backend="physx_cpu". The GR00T evaluation loop also requires num_eval_envs == 1. These are properties of the inspected native-scene evaluation path.

Run separate processes for disjoint tasks, backgrounds or episode-seed shards. General ManiSkill GPU-vectorized training capabilities do not establish vectorized support in this factory. For other training paths, inspect the algorithm's own environment and reset semantics before changing its environment count.

Plan and shard scene previews

Research checkout required

The module examples on this page require an asset-complete research checkout, its compatible Python environment, and the relevant simulator or model dependencies. The current public repository ↗ contains a README, license and repository metadata; cloning it does not provide the task modules, robot assets, datasets or checkpoints used below. These examples document the verified research interfaces.

python utils/scene_matrix.py plan --out output/scene90

python utils/scene_matrix.py preview \
  --out output/scene90/preview --shard 0 --shards 3 --resume

python utils/scene_matrix.py preview \
  --out output/scene90/preview --shard 1 --shards 3 --resume

python utils/scene_matrix.py preview \
  --out output/scene90/preview --shard 2 --shards 3 --resume

The three shard commands may run in separate terminals on a prepared machine. They are placement previews, not policy evaluation jobs. The preview tool isolates child asset caches; its resume logic checks passed records against source hashes and seeds. Retain failed logs for inspection.

Partition policy work explicitly

For policy sweeps, create a manifest with a unique tuple of task ID, background ID and episode seed for every planned episode. Assign each tuple to one worker, give workers distinct output directories, and pin the same checkpoint, adapter, task revision, camera profile and instruction rule.

Keep renderer/device allocation explicit when several CPU-physics processes share a GPU for rendering or inference. Begin with a small number of workers and measure memory use before expanding. Process parallelism does not remove model or renderer resource requirements.

Merge episodes before calculating scores

Verify that all planned tuples are present exactly once. Keep runtime errors distinguishable from task failures and preserve enough logs to reproduce each one. A resumed run must not mix old and new checkpoints or task fingerprints.

Calculate per-stage success from the merged episode records, then aggregate according to the score protocol. Averaging worker percentages can weight unequal shards incorrectly. Save the original plan, each worker's records and the final aggregation script as part of the reproduction package.
